name: Ola Wójcik
role: Data analyst at a logistics company
quote: I didn't know “data analyst” was a job until I was 17.
intro: Our ICT teacher looked after three schools at once. She still found a minute to send me one link — and that link opened everything else.

started.title: Free online spreadsheet & SQL course
started.text: Two evenings a week on my mum's laptop. For practice I analysed our town's bus timetable and found two buses that never had passengers.

started.title: Student hackathon in Lublin
started.text: Our team of four built a map of empty classrooms. We didn't win, but a mentor told me about a data scholarship.

started.title: Scholarship for women in STEM
started.text: It covered my first year of studies in Wrocław — and a laptop that didn't overheat.

helpers: My ICT teacher, who sent the first link

name: Jakub Nowicki
role: Backend developer at a fintech startup
quote: I learned to code on a school computer during lunch breaks.
intro: We had no computer at home, so the school lab was my place. Twenty minutes a day turned out to be enough to start.

started.title: Free JavaScript course for beginners
started.text: I saved lessons to a USB stick and read them on the bus. My first project was a calculator that could only add.

started.title: Regional programming contest
started.text: I came 14th out of 60. An online coach from the contest kept sending me tasks for a year.

started.title: Weekend hackathon in Rzeszów
started.text: We built a parking app. A company there offered me my first summer internship.

helpers: An older cousin studying in Kraków
The school caretaker who let me stay late

name: Marta Zielińska
role: UX/UI designer at a software house
quote: Drawing in the margins of my notebook turned out to be a skill.
intro: I thought design meant painting. Then I discovered that someone designs every button I tap — and that I could be that person.

started.title: Online course: UI design basics
started.text: Free, in English, with subtitles. I redesigned our school's website as homework nobody asked for.

started.title: App redesign competition for students
started.text: My redesign of a local bus app won second place. The prize was a mentoring month with a designer.

started.title: Design summer school scholarship
started.text: Two weeks in Gdańsk, fully paid. I met my first employer there.

helpers: My art teacher, who said “try it digitally”
A designer mentor from the competition

name: Natalia Kaczmarek
quote: I was the only girl in the after-school club. Now I lead a team.
intro: Maths was my thing, but no one around me used it for anything except exams. AI showed me where maths actually lives.

started.title: Online maths & Python for beginners
started.text: I combined the two: a tiny program that predicted my grades. It was wrong, and that made me curious.

started.title: AI hackathon in Poznań
started.text: Our model sorted recycling from photos. We won our category, and I stopped thinking “this isn't for me”.

started.title: Exchange semester scholarship
started.text: Six months abroad in a research lab. I came back knowing exactly what I wanted to do.

helpers: A physics teacher who lent me books

name: Bartosz Lis
role: Game developer at an indie studio
quote: My first game had one level and three bugs per pixel.
intro: I went to a vocational school as an IT technician. Everyone said real game studios were for kids from big cities.

started.title: Free game-development video tutorials
started.text: I followed them line by line, then broke everything on purpose to understand it.

started.title: 48-hour game jam in Białystok
started.text: Our game about a lost bison got the audience award. Someone from a studio played it twice.

started.title: Local foundation grant for vocational students
started.text: It paid for a better graphics card and a trip to a games conference.

helpers: My vocational school teacher, who let me use the lab

name: Zuzanna Mazur
quote: I wanted to be a doctor. Now I help hospitals plan with data.
intro: I loved biology and was scared of computers. It turns out you can care about people and write code at the same time.

started.title: Statistics competition for secondary schools
started.text: We counted how many students skip breakfast. Our poster made it to the national final.

started.title: Online course: data analysis with Python
started.text: Hard at first. I watched each video twice and asked questions in the course forum.

started.title: Health-data hackathon in Wrocław
started.text: We predicted queues at an emergency room. A hospital still uses a version of our idea.

helpers: A data scientist I met at the hackathon

name: Igor Pawlak
role: AI researcher at a university lab
quote: Nobody around me worked in tech. The internet did.
intro: My parents run a small shop. Tech felt like a different planet — until I found people online who explained it patiently.

started.title: Free online intro to machine learning
started.text: I understood maybe 30% the first time. The second time, 70%.

started.title: National AI challenge for schools
started.text: Our team taught a robot to recognise road signs. We came third.

started.title: University scholarship for students from small towns
started.text: It meant I could study in Toruń without working nights.

helpers: My ICT teacher, who registered our team

name: Weronika Dudek
role: Product designer at a travel startup
quote: I started at a vocational school — graphic design technician.
intro: People told me vocational school closes doors. For me it opened the first one: I had real clients at 17.

started.title: School media club
started.text: We made posters and videos for the town's events. My first ‘client’ was the local library.

started.title: Design hackathon in Kraków
started.text: We designed a mountain-safety app. A startup founder was on the jury.

started.title: Online course: accessible design
started.text: I learned to design for everyone, including my grandma. Now it's my favourite topic.

helpers: A startup founder from the jury
